title: Avoid Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drainage Lines
description: Using a sanitary tee on a horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that causes frequent line blockages. Sanitary tees are designed specifically for transitions from horizontal to vertical flow or for venting connections. When installed horizontally, the sharp sweep fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the direction of flow, leading to solids accumulating at the junction. Instead, standard code principles require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep fitting for horizontal-to-horizontal flow transitions. Installing the correct directional fitting maintains flow velocity and prevents unnecessary drainage service calls.

Avoid Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drainage Lines

Using a sanitary tee on a horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that causes frequent line blockages. Sanitary tees are designed specifically for transitions from horizontal to vertical flow or for venting connections. When installed horizontally, the sharp sweep fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the direction of flow, leading to solids accumulating at the junction. Instead, standard code principles require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep fitting for horizontal-to-horizontal flow transitions. Installing the correct directional fitting maintains flow velocity and prevents unnecessary drainage service calls.
